title: How to run Evals at Scale: Thinking beyond Accuracy or Similarity — Muktesh Mishra, Adobe

summary: Muktesh Mishra, lead engineer for applied AI for developer platforms at Adobe and co-author of a CI/CD design patterns book, addresses how to run evals at scale for AI applications. He frames evals as the fundamental approach for writing test cases to measure AI applications, essential because LLMs are nondeterministic—outputs vary for the same input, and prompt changes can break behavior unpredictably. Without measurement, business impact, system-goal alignment, continuous improvement, and user trust all suffer. He stresses data as foundational to evals. Approaches include starting small with synthetic or artificial data, continuously observing and refining datasets, labeling data to cover multiple flows and application aspects, and maintaining multiple datasets rather than a single one—because one dataset is never sufficient. For what to evaluate, he recommends defining goals and objectives, designing modular components, optimizing data handling, and testing flows, outputs, and paths. On adaptive evals, he underscores that there is no universal eval. A typical RAG or Q&A application may use accuracy, similarity, or usefulness metrics, while code generation requires measuring functional correctness and robustness against an actual codebase. Agent evaluation involves trajectory evaluation (which path the agent takes), multi-turn simulation for complex conversations, and tool-call correctness or test-suite validation. For scaling evals, he recommends catching intermediate results and regressions, focusing on orchestration and parallelism, aggregating results, running frequently, and following a measure-monitor-analyze-repeat cycle. He notes there is no fixed strategy—teams should balance human-in-loop versus automation, trading off speed versus fidelity, and rely on process over tools since tools cannot automate everything. He coins "eval-driven development" as the AI analog of test-driven development.
